results.title: Z.ai: Official Playground for High-Performance GLM Models | Product Hunt
results.content:
What do you think? …

Rohan Chaubey

GLM-Legal is Z.ai’s legal AI model, built on GLM-5.3-Flash and trained for agentic legal work. That means multi-step tasks like contract review, evidence analysis and compliance research. It’s in an application-only API beta.

Problem: Legal work is long, detailed and unforgiving. A contract review or compliance check has many steps, and one missed point can sink the result. General-purpose models often fall short on that kind of multi-step legal work.

Solution: Z.ai took its GLM-5.3-Flash model and trained it for legal tasks. Per Z.ai, that meant legal mid-training on a larger corpus, then reinforcement learning across tens of thousands of legal task environments. It built the agent harness alongside the model, so the two were improved together. [...] Who it’s for: law firms, in-house counsel and compliance teams exploring AI for legal workflows. This is a tool for professionals and doesn’t replace legal advice or a lawyer.

Read Z.ai’s announcement · See the Vals AI results · Apply for API access

M.Cevheri BOZOGLAN

#### What's great

I've been using GLM-5.2 extensively over the past few days, primarily for software engineering tasks through OpenCode and Hermes-Agent, and it has genuinely impressed me.

The biggest compliment I can give is that, during many coding sessions, it gave me a similar feeling to using Claude Opus. Not because the models are identical, but because of how reliably it understands context, follows complex instructions, and completes multi-step engineering tasks. [...] How it performs:

Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark: 19.17% of tasks passed, up from 6.67% for the base model. A task only passes if every one of its criteria passes, so even the top scores are low in absolute terms.

LegalBench: 86.23%, versus 88.56% for Claude Fable 5. Z.ai says it matches frontier models here, but its numbers show it slightly behind.

Cost: about $0.15 per Harvey LAB test on Vals AI’s runs, much lower than the other models compared. The price Vals used isn’t a published GLM-Legal price.

Access:

API: It’s an application-only beta, with no published price

Weights: no public weights reported, and no Hugging Face repo yet

Desktop: Z.ai says it’s coming to its AutoClaw desktop agent app, with no date given

results.title: Opper AI Reviews (2026) | Product Hunt
results.content:
### Top forum threads

Ulykbek Asylbek

#### What's great

The "one sub-processor covers every model" detail is the actual unlock here - anyone who's tried to get a GDPR-conscious AI stack signed off by legal knows the real bottleneck isn't picking a good model, it's getting a dozen separate DPAs approved for a dozen separate providers. Collapsing that into one sub-processor while still giving access to 30+ providers is solving the boring-but-critical part nobody else seems to prioritize.

#### What needs improvement

Curious how the per-team spend caps and audit trails hold up once an

agent is calling multiple models in a single task autonomously - does

a spend cap trigger mid-chain and fail gracefully, or does it need to [...] be checked before each individual model call? That failure mode seems

important for anything running unattended in production.

#### vs Alternatives

Looked at OpenRouter for the same "one key, many models" idea, but it

doesn't solve the EU data residency or single-sub-processor angle at

all. For anyone building in Europe who actually needs to answer "where

does this data go" to a legal or compliance team, that's the whole

ballgame, not just a nice-to-have.
